name: Invalid string escape
description: Flags a C-like escape such as \n, \t, or \r inside a string literal, since Papyrus stores those as literal backslash-plus-letter characters rather than whitespace.
definition:
Flags, as a `[warning]`, a string literal that contains a C-like escape sequence from the high-signal set `
`, `	`, or ``. Papyrus string literals have no escape sequences: a literal `"
"` is the two characters backslash and `n`, not a newline, so authors coming from C/JavaScript/Python who write `Debug.Trace("Loaded
Done")` or `"	"` expecting whitespace get the backslash characters in the stored string instead. Only those three letters are checked, to avoid noise from intentional Windows-style paths that contain other backslash-letter pairs (`"C:\Games"`) or doubled backslashes; `\`, `"`, and a backslash before any other letter are left alone. The diagnostic names the escape that was found and explains that Papyrus does not interpret it. Prefer separate `Debug.Trace` calls (or a real newline in the source between concatenated string literals, if the compiler accepts that) over embedding escape sequences. Not auto-fixable: the author's intent — a real newline, a literal backslash, or something else — cannot be inferred safely.
